set.body:
Objective
Make ScalaFIM multivar mathematically defensible for structured low-rank modeling by combining the duality/operator core with Allen-style sparse-functional factors and Udell-style generalized observation models.

Constitutional rules
- One public model maps to one explicit formula, estimand, symmetry class, solver theorem, certificate, and oracle suite.
- Anchor regularization is never named or documented as jointly estimated sparse or functional PCA.
- Geometry Q/R, observation loss, structural penalty, constraint, and missingness mechanism remain distinct typed concepts.
- Global, epsilon-global, stationary, coordinatewise-stationary, feasible, and unresolved results are never conflated.
- All preprocessing, graph estimation, loss scaling, rank selection, and hyperparameter tuning are fold-local through ModelSpec.
- Shared implementations remain portable and warning-clean on JVM and Scala.js.
- APIs use precise Scala 3 ADTs, opaque validated scalars, smart constructors, exhaustive matches, and evidence-bearing capabilities; invalid theorem claims should be unrepresentable.

Epic acceptance
1. A checked mathematical contract and capability matrix cover every supported estimator.
2. Sparse plus quadratic smoothness, sparse plus TV, and multiblock variants have exact executable objectives.
3. Joint sparse-functional factorization is distinct from anchor refinement and has honest nonconvex guarantees.
4. Generalized losses, observation masks, partial latent encoding, and missingness semantics are typed and fold-safe.
5. Certificates bind program, data/mask, operators, parameters, assumptions, solver configuration, and achieved residuals or gaps.
6. Analytic, differential, metamorphic, adversarial, regression, and performance tests cover every solver path.
7. Both multivar and multivar-ir pass on JVM and JS; final compileAll testAll passes from a clean detached worktree.
8. Documentation includes equations, theorem map, counterexamples, unsupported cases, reproducibility fixtures, and external-review questions.

Primary references
- Allen and Weylandt, Sparse and Functional PCA.
- Allen, Grosenick, and Taylor, Generalized Least Squares Matrix Decomposition.
- Udell, Horn, Zadeh, and Boyd, Generalized Low Rank Models.
- Tseng block coordinate descent, PALM, FISTA, and Chambolle-Pock as applicable.
set.title: EPIC: mathematically defensible structured generalized low-rank multivar
